subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for the deep dive this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps based on what you shared:

What I heard:
- Production traffic: ~50 requests/sec peak, ~30 req/s sustained; average request ~512 tokens (prompt+response).
- Latency SLO: p50 ~80–120ms, p95 < 250ms for user-facing flows.
- Throughput requirement: bursts to 80–100 req/s for batch ingestion windows.
- Data sensitivity: PCI-adjacent but we can run with hosted offering if we have a clear data retention policy; you asked about VPC/private if needed later.

Recommendation: Dedicated capacity.
- Given the p50/p95 targets and 50+ req/s sustained with bursts, a reserved GPU pool will give predictable latency and isolation. Hosted API could work for quick proof-of-concept but will likely see higher jitter under bursty traffic; Dedicated lets us reserve capacity and configure autoscaling and burst policies.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll send a short capacity worksheet (attached) to capture your traffic profile and token distribution. Can you confirm the 512-token average and share any 95th percentile token lengths?
2) Schedule a short perf test (we can simulate 50–100 req/s with your sample prompts) — would Wednesday or Thursday this week work?
3) If perf looks good we'll put together a Dedicated sizing + pricing estimate (PO-ready).

Attaching: redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-worksheet.pdf and a sample capacity estimate.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers from our side:
- Average request size is 480–520 tokens (we'll provide a sample set).
- Peak burst windows hit ~90 req/s for ~5–10 minutes during business hours.
- Latency target is strict for the customer-facing chat: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 250ms. For async batch scoring we can tolerate higher latency.

I agree Dedicated sounds like the most predictable option. Two questions before we move to sizing:
1) For Dedicated, can you confirm typical cluster configs you recommend for 50–100 req/s at ~512 tokens (GPU types / reserved nodes)?
2) How long does provisioning take and what’s the minimum commitment?

We can do a perf test on Thursday at 10:00am PT — Tom and I will join. We'll also upload a small sample of production prompts to the shared Drive link.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of AI Platform | FinPay

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up

Alyssa — great, thanks for the confirmations and for scheduling Thursday 10am PT. Quick answers to your questions and what I'll bring to the perf call:

1) Typical Dedicated sizing guidance (ballpark for your profile):
   - 50–100 req/s @ ~512 tokens: we usually recommend a reserved pool equivalent to 3–5 x A100-80GB (or 4–8 x A10s depending on model & quantization).
   - Autoscaling configured to maintain p95 latency under load; we size the base pool for sustained throughput and allow short bursts with a small buffer.
   - If you plan to run larger context windows or multi-turn chat with long KV caches, factor +1 GPU for cache-heavy workloads.

2) Provisioning & commitment:
   - Provisioning: Dedicated private pools can be provisioned in ~24–72 hours in hosted regions; for private VPC it may take longer depending on network approvals.
   - Minimum commitment: monthly reserved capacity contracts are common; we can do a 3-month pilot with monthly billing to start if you prefer.

What I'll bring to the perf test:
- A perf harness that will replay your sample prompts and measure p50/p95/p99 under configurable concurrency.
- A draft capacity estimate (attached) that maps node counts to expected latency and cost.

Next steps: I'll upload an updated capacity-estimate.xlsx to the Drive and loop in Marissa for the pricing/contract side after the test.

Cheers,
Dylan

Looping in pricing & ops —

Great to see alignment on Dedicated. A few operational notes so the perf test can lead straight into an agreement if results look good:

- I'll prepare a pilot quote (3-month reserved capacity) based on the attached estimate. Please confirm whether you want a hard reserved pool (guaranteed nodes) vs a blended reserved+burst approach — we can model both.
- For procurement: we typically need a signed SOW/PO; I can send a draft SOW after the perf test with estimated monthly costs and hit/miss SLAs.
- Ops will require firewall/VPC peering details if you want Private VPC; otherwise Dedicated hosted pools run in our secure tenant with SOC2 controls.

Action items:
- Alyssa / Tom: upload sample prompts and a 24h traffic histogram to the Drive link before 10am PT Thursday.

- Marissa: draft pilot SOW and pricing (will send within 48 hours of perf results).
